proposal.label: Construction material price index (annual)
proposal.rationale: Construction input costs (ready mixed concrete) influence the supply-side cost of delivering housing. Higher construction input prices increase building costs, which may be passed through to sales prices and rents, especially in supply-constrained markets. This is a direct cost-push indicator for the realised housing costs channel.

proposal.label: Foreign workforce (excluding domestic workers)
proposal.rationale: Foreign workers constitute a significant portion of Singapore's rental market demand. Increases in foreign workforce numbers directly expand the pool of potential renters, exerting upward pressure on rents, particularly in lower- and middle-cost rental segments where foreign workers live. This is distinct from the non-resident population channel which captures PR/other foreign persons; this focuses specifically on work permit holders as a housing demand component.

proposal.label: Share of work permit holders in non-resident population
proposal.rationale: Work permit holders (CMP and non-CMP) represent a large segment of the foreign population that rents in Singapore, primarily in HDB flats. Their presence directly drives rental demand. Tracking this share provides a cleaner signal than total non-resident population, which also includes tourists, PRs, and other categories less relevant to housing demand. Rising work permit shares indicate tighter restrictions easing or increased inflow, boosting rental demand.

proposal.label: Median household employment income (annual)
proposal.rationale: Median household income from work is a proxy for the purchasing power and affordability constraints of resident households. Higher incomes expand demand for sales housing (especially owner-occupied) and increase ability to pay rents. This complements GDP in the Income and activity channel by directly measuring household-level income, which better captures mortgage repayment capacity and rental budget constraints at the micro level. The median is less volatile and more representative than averages.
